calling the updateNodeRunnerWhitelistStatus function executes require(isNodeRunnerWhitelisted[_nodeRunner] != isNodeRunnerWhitelisted[_nodeRunner], ...), which always reverts, the DAO is unable to whitelist any trusted node runners

rotateNodeRunnerOfSmartWallet function provides the only way to set bannedNodeRunners to true... before the node runner calls the registerBLSPublicKeys function to create a smart wallet, calling the rotateNodeRunnerOfSmartWallet function reverts. Mitigation: A function... that can directly set bannedNodeRunners for a node runner can be added

There is a require in _assertUserHasEnoughGiantLPToClaimVaultLP(): require(lpTokenETH.lastInteractedTimestamp(msg.sender) + 1 days < block.timestamp, "Too new")... a user can perform withdrawDETH or withdrawLPTokens of one LPToken only once a day, others more will fail

_dao is not required to be an address that corresponds to a governance contract... When the DAO becomes compromised or malicious, the actions of the node runners, who are not malicious, can be restricted at the DAO's will... a compromised or malicious DAO can cause severe consequences, including ETH losses

Current implementation of functions add, remove, buy and sell first transfer fractional tokens, and then base tokens. If this base token is ERC777... we can re call buy function with the same balance of base token, but with different fractional balance. Recommended: Add openzeppelin nonReentrant modifier.

The Pair contract does not allow users to submit a deadline for their action. This missing feature enables pending transactions to be maliciously executed at a later point. Recommended: Introduce a deadline parameter to the mentioned functions.

the formula incorrectly calculates the price to be represented in whatever number of decimals the base token is in. Since there are many common base tokens (such as USDC) that will have fewer than 18 decimals, this will create a large mismatch between expected prices and the prices that result from the function.

The function buyQuote() calculates the amount of base tokens required... this function rounds down the required amount, which is in favor of the buyer... it might be possible to receive free fractional tokens. Recommended: round up the required amount.

anyone can swap their NFT token id with another NFT token id without paying any fee(both ids should be whitelisted). it's swap without fee... attacker can swap his NFT token for all the NFT balance of contract and steal those NFT tokens airdrop all in one transaction.

An attacker may manipulate the price of a pair by transferring tokens directly to the pair. Since the Pair contract exposes the price function, it maybe be used as a price oracle in third-party integrations. Manipulating the price of a pair may allow an attacker to steal funds from such integrations.

When a Vault owner creates/adds a reward token to the Staking contract with faulty escrow config parameters, the reward tokens sent to the Staking contract will forever be locked up. This can happen since there are no validity checks on the values of the Escrow config for the reward tokens

It uses Math.Rounding.Down, but it should use Math.Rounding.Up ... The value would be rounded round to zero. This will be the amount of shares burned from users account, which is zero. Hence user can drain the assets from the vault without burning their shares.

Attacker can steal 99% of the balance of a reward token of any Staking contract... As long as attacker is creator of a Vault that has the target Staking contract attached to it, attacker can call changeStakingRewardSpeeds to modify the rewardSpeeds... There are no checks for limits on the rewardsPerSecond value

The current implementation does not check if the _beefyBooster is legitimate or not, and worse, it _beefyVault.approve to the _beefyBooster during initialization... This malicious _beefyBooster can execute _beefyVault.transferFrom(BeefyAdapter), and take all the tokens stored by the adapter

Anyone who uses same adapter has the ability to pause it... in case if you are creator of vault that uses adaptor that you want to pause, then you are able to pause it... attacker is able to pause adapterA and as result it's not possible to deposit anymore

the new end time is calculated based off of the balance of the reward token owned by the contract. This, however, is not the same as the number of reward tokens that are left to be distributed since some of those tokens may be owed to users who have not collected their rewards yet

Reward deltaIndex in _accrueRewards() is multiplied by 10**decimals() but eventually divided by rewards.ONE (which is equal to 10**IERC20Metadata(address(rewardToken)).decimals()) in _accrueUser(). If the number of decimals in MultiRewardEscrow share token differs from the number of decimals in the reward token, then all rewards are multipled by 10 ** (decimals() - rewardToken.decimals())

every time when deposit, mint, withdraw is called, highWaterMark is updated to the new state, so protocol doesn't track yield progress anymore... anyone can frontrun takeFees and deposit small amount of assets in order to update highWaterMark, so protocol will not get any fees

Anyone can deploy a Vault with a malicious Staking contract attached. If the Staking contract already exists, we can just pass its address to deployVault and no checks will be applied to see whether the Staking contract matches valid Staking templates in the Template Registry.
the rewards are never accrued and the resulting staking rewards are lost forever. This is because accrueRewards is called on caller and receiver but never owner.

Because AdapterBase calls the Strategy using delegatecall, the Strategy has access to the calling contract's storage and can be manipulated directly... a MaliciousStrategy ... will manipulate the performanceFee and highWaterMark values. Of course, any other storage slots of the adapter could also be manipulated.

the maxLoss input is not specified when calling the Yearn vault's withdraw function ... calling the Vault.withdraw or Vault.redeem function will always revert ... As a result, users lose the deposited assets that they are unable to withdraw.

ERC4626 standard requires maxWithdraw to return the maximum amount of underlying assets that can be withdrawn ... withdraw in Vault implements a fee which is not calculated in maxWithdraw ... upstream contracts that call maxWithdraw and use the return value for withdraw will always revert.

In case the swap operation failed... the code that swallows the error: ...if err != nil { logger.Error(...) }. Notice that in case of an error, swappedAmount will still be written to. Later... convertCoin := sdk.NewCoin(..., transferredCoin.Amount.Sub(swappedAmount)). ...variables returned in error states should not be trusted and should be overwritten.

H-01 Lack of Balance Validation: '_checkBalances() is only used in _swap() and _lpTokenSpecified(). There is no balance validation for depositGivenInputAmount() and withdrawGivenOutputAmount()... user deposits/withdrawls may break the invariant'. Assessed type: Invalid Validation

There is no way to revoke the approval which given via DelegateToken.approve(address,delegateTokenId)... Even after revoking the approval for operator using setApprovalAll this msg.sender == readApproved(...) will be true and able to call transferFrom. Assessed type: Access Control

CreateOfferer.sol should not enforce the nonce incremented sequentially... the nonce tracked by CreateOfferer.sol internally is out of sync with the contract nonce in seaport contract forever. Then the CreateOfferer.sol is not usable because... transaction revert in this check: if (nonce.value != contractNonce) revert InvalidContractNonce. Assessed type: DoS

The function checks if winning tickets for the prize index 0 have been set by verifying that winningTickets[currentRound_][0].length == 0... but it does not account for prizes with higher indices that may already have been distributed. As a result, users can still enter tickets after some prizes have been distributed

the claimPrizesForRound() function always transfers the full prize amounts to the first caller, regardless of the number of winners for the prize... the amount pulled from the owner can simply be scaled by the number of winners: WETH.transferFrom(_from, address(this), _amountWETH * _numWinners)

the ThrusterPoolDeployer contains a flaw in the implementation of claimGas()... The function attempts to claim gas for the zero address (address(0)) instead of the deployer's own address (address(this))... the IBlast.claimMaxGas() call will always fail when provided with the zero address

in case if yield cut will be changed for a pool, then protocol fee should be minted for previous period using old yield cut, otherwise the yield cut will be incorrect... Impact: Yield can be collected with wrong proportion

userTotalStaked invariant will be broken ... in release() flow due to userTotalStaked is not updated together with selfStakes[address].amount or communityStakes[address][x].amount. The judge: 'due to incorrect accounting, userTotalStaked may end up being less than intended, causing a loss of funds'; Gitcoin: 'fixes the userTotalStaked invariant (accounting error)'.

The _doCheckValueType function ... contains reversed comparison logic for the gte and lte operators. This reversal causes the function to perform the opposite checks than intended, potentially allowing operations to pass validation when they should fail.

the underlying function performing the call assumes that any exceptions (from Lido) will be bubbled up, but with call being a low level rather than a Solidity function, it is not the case ... payable(address(stEth)).call{value: _initialETH}(""); ... Reverts are not bubbled up

YieldStakingBase uses the returned shares value from depositing as if they were assets... But then, it calculates totalAssets to compute the yield using the actual ETH balance... the borrowed amount and the yield amount will differ significantly.
The current implementation just restricts onBehalf!=address(0) and does not restrict onBehalf == nftOwner. This way, we can maliciously specify onBehalf!=nftOwner ... resulting in an underflow.
there is a missing check on msg.sender in isolate liquidation flow, which allows anyone to take the collateral NFT token... Assessed type: Access Control
the user's yieldAccount is not compatible with _safeMint because the implementation YieldAcount.sol doesn't have onERC721Received method required by _safeMint... no one can unstake.
passing totalBorrowAmount to erc20TransferOutBidAmountToLiqudity()... Recommended Mitigation: Just decrease assetData.totalBidAmout by vars.totalBidAmount (fix passes the correct parameter).

msg.sender is used to fetch borrower yield account address... vars.yieldAccout = IYieldAccount(yieldAccounts[msg.sender]); the protocol will attempt to use botAdmin yield account address instead of the borrower account... transaction failure.

There are two checks on price staleness in PriceOracle::getAssetPriceFromChainlink, but both checks are invalid. updatedAt should be used to check if the answer is within the heartbeat... answeredInRound is deprecated.

the borrow interest compounding implementation will not factor in the duration of pausing... Interests continuously compound with no repayment allowed. When unpaused, many accounts are vulnerable to immediate liquidation.

M-03: 'the previous bidder's bid amount is returned. Because previous bidder is blacklisted... erc20TransferOutBidAmount(...) will revert the auction tx. At this point, no one can bid on the loan.' Also remain-amount transfer to a blacklisted borrower reverts liquidation.

M-06: 'YieldEthStakingLido lacks a limit on the max stake amount... If the stake amount exceeds this value, it will not be possible to unstake() and the token will be locked' (MAX_STETH_WITHDRAWAL_AMOUNT).

InterestLogic.updateInterestRates(poolData, debtAssetData, (vars.totalBorrowAmount + vars.totalExtraAmount), 0) ... (vars.totalBorrowAmount + vars.totalExtraAmount) is incorrect input, which inflates liquidityAdded ... and deflates utilization rate ... This will cause an inflated borrow rate/supply rate

the protocol will attempt to collect extraAmount from the position owner, but he may revoke ERC20 approval and cancel the safeTransferFrom function call. As a result, nftDebt will not be repaid and will continue to collect interest, increasing the protocol's losses.

The new feeFactor will be applied to interest collected before the feeFactor was updated ... But the protocol will still use the old supply rate that was calculated using the previous feeFactor. This may cause inconsistencies in the fee accounting for the protocol.

After updating the interest model, the protocol does not update the interest rate, resulting in interest being calculated at the old model rates for some time ... interest will be calculated with the cached old model rates until InterestLogic.updateInterestRates is finally called.

The unchecked multiplication of int32 values (rs and rt) and type conversion within the execute function in MIPS contract can result in an overflow, leading to the assignment of an incorrect value to the val variable... it was converted to type uint32 even though the value might have gone above it (Assessed type: Under/Overflow).

the address must be naturally aligned. If the least-significant bit of the address is non-zero, an Address Error exception occurs. However, in the contract, the address is not checked. (sponsor: 'does not check for half-word alignment within the LH and LHU instruction implementations').

anyone can call the loadPrecompilePreimagePart() to load data into the contract. The problem is that anyone is able to specify the address _precompile parameter. This opens up the door for malicious users to pre-populate data and use it to validate wrong data... a malicious user can set preimagePartOk[_key][_offset] = true.

The readMem() and writeMem() functions do not properly validate the memory address being accessed... The function only checks for 4-byte alignment but does not validate if the address is within the allowed memory range... possibly then allowing access to the entire 4GB address space.
